solutions.latex:
Method 1

$S_1+S_2=\displaystyle\int_0^1(1-x^2)\,dx=\left[x-\dfrac{x^3}{3}\right]_0^1=\left(1-\dfrac{1}{3}\right)-(0-0)=\dfrac{2}{3}$

But $S_1=S_2\Rightarrow 2S_1=\dfrac{2}{3}$, $S_1=S_2=\dfrac{1}{3}$

$S_1=\displaystyle\int_0^{\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+a}}}(-x^2+1-ax^2)\,dx=\int_0^{\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+a}}}\left(1-(1+a)x^2\right)dx=\left[x-\dfrac{1+a}{3}x^3\right]_0^{\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+a}}}$

$=\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1+a}}-\dfrac{1+a}{3}\cdot\dfrac{1}{(1+a)\sqrt{1+a}}\right)-0=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1+a}}\left(1-\dfrac{1+a}{3(1+a)}\right)$

$\Rightarrow\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1+a}}\left(1-\dfrac{1+a}{3(1+a)}\right)=\dfrac{1}{3}$

$2(1+a)=(1+a)\sqrt{1+a}$

$4(1+a)^2=(1+a)^2(1+a)$

$(1+a)^2(1+a)-4(1+a)^2=0$, $(1+a)^2(1+a-4)=0$

$a=-1$ or $a=3$; $a>0\Rightarrow a=3$

Method 2

$S_2=\displaystyle\int_0^1(1-x^2)\,dx-S_1$; $S_1=S_2$, $\therefore 2S_1=\int_0^1(1-x^2)\,dx$, $S_1=\dfrac{1}{2}\int_0^1(1-x^2)\,dx$, similar to Method 1.

Method 3

$S_1=\dfrac{2(1+a)}{3(1+a)\sqrt{1+a}}$ (as above)

$S_2=\displaystyle\int_0^{\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+a}}}ax^2\,dx+\int_{\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+a}}}^1(1-x^2)\,dx=\left[\dfrac{a}{3}x^3\right]_0^{\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+a}}}+\left[x-\dfrac{x^3}{3}\right]_{\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+a}}}^1$

$=\dfrac{a}{3(1+a)\sqrt{1+a}}+\left(1-\dfrac{1}{3}\right)-\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1+a}}-\dfrac{1}{3(1+a)\sqrt{1+a}}\right)=\dfrac{2}{3}-\dfrac{2+2a}{3(1+a)\sqrt{1+a}}$

Equating $S_1$ and $S_2$: $\dfrac{2(1+a)}{3(1+a)\sqrt{1+a}}=\dfrac{2}{3}-\dfrac{2(1+a)}{3(1+a)\sqrt{1+a}}$

$\dfrac{2(1+a)}{(1+a)\sqrt{1+a}}=1$, $2(1+a)=(1+a)\sqrt{1+a}$, $4(1+a)^2=(1+a)^3$

$(1+a)^2(a-3)=0$; $a=-1$ (outside domain), $\therefore a=3$
solutions.marks_breakdown: No mark allocation shown in the source (three methods given); answer a = 3
review_reasons: source gives three methods but no marking criteria for this part

solutions.latex:
$AP=\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{\sin\theta}$

$PC=CD-DP=2-\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{\tan\theta}-1\right)=3-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{\tan\theta}$

Total cost $C=100\,000\,AP+80\,000\,PC$

$C=100\,000\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{\sin\theta}+80\,000\left(3-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{\tan\theta}\right)=100\,000\sqrt{3}(\sin\theta)^{-1}+240\,000-80\,000\sqrt{3}(\tan\theta)^{-1}$

$C'=\dfrac{-100\,000\sqrt{3}\cos\theta}{\sin^2\theta}+\dfrac{80\,000\sqrt{3}\sec^2\theta}{\tan^2\theta}=\dfrac{-100\,000\sqrt{3}\cos\theta}{\sin^2\theta}+\dfrac{80\,000\sqrt{3}}{\sin^2\theta}$

$\left(\text{since }\dfrac{\sec^2\theta}{\tan^2\theta}=\dfrac{1}{\cos^2\theta}\times\dfrac{\cos^2\theta}{\sin^2\theta}=\dfrac{1}{\sin^2\theta}\right)$

Let $C'=0$: $-100\,000\sqrt{3}\cos\theta+80\,000\sqrt{3}=0$, $\cos\theta=\dfrac{80\,000\sqrt{3}}{100\,000\sqrt{3}}=\dfrac{4}{5}$, $\theta\approx 36.9^\circ$

$$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}\theta & 36^\circ & \cos^{-1}\left(\frac{4}{5}\right) & 37^\circ\\\hline C' & -4520 & 0 & 652\end{array}$$

$\therefore$ minimum turning point when $\cos\theta=\dfrac{4}{5}$
